Where to Stay in Nan?
10 Hotels We've Reviewed

heroSub: Ten Nan hotels across every budget — minimalist boutiques in the historic Old City, rice-terrace resorts up in Pua, riverside villas in the Bo Kluea valley, down to hostels from ฿99. Covering the three main bases: Nan town, Pua, and Bo Kluea. Starting from around ฿99–2,800/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right base in Nan matter?
introHtml: Nan looks like a small town, but its sights are spread far apart. The Old City (Nai Wiang) is the hub — Wat Phumin, the museum, the walking street, all walkable in a day. But Pua district sits about 60 km from town, a zone of stepped rice terraces and the gateway up Doi Phu Kha. And Bo Kluea lies another ~80 km out, a deep valley famous for its ancient salt wells. Many people book a hotel without thinking about which zone they'll explore, then end up driving hours back and forth each day. This guide rounds up 10 Nan hotels we've picked across every tier — from Old City boutiques to rice-view resorts in Pua, down to value hostels — each with an honest take from real reviews, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Nan has no metro and very little public transport in town — renting a car or motorbike is by far the most practical option, especially if you plan to head up to Pua or Bo Kluea. Within the Old City you'll find a few tuk-tuks and songthaews, but they're hard to flag down in the evening. Nan Nakhon Airport (NNT) is only about 10 minutes from town. The main bases in this guide: Old City / Nai Wiang — Wat Phumin, the Nan museum, the walking street · Pua district — stepped rice terraces, the road up Doi Phu Kha, Wat Phuket · Bo Kluea — ancient salt wells, mountain valleys, mountain roads.

entries.name: Nan Nakara Boutique Hotel
entries.revCount: 64 reviews · highest score in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old City Nan · walk to Wat Phumin & the walking street
entries.addr: 16/6 Soi 1, Phakong Rd, Nai Wiang, Mueang Nan
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this list at 9.6 — Nan Nakara is a minimalist boutique right in the historic Old City, an easy walk from Wat Phumin and the Friday–Saturday walking street. Rooms are done in calm tones with a clear split between living and sleeping zones, plus a rain shower. Real reviews praise the cleanliness and the location where everything is close on foot — a good fit if you want to soak up the Old City at walking pace.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a small property and fills up on walking-street nights, so book ahead for Friday–Saturday and ask for an upper-floor room for a quieter stay.
pros: Old City location, walk to Wat Phumin and the walking street
Clean minimalist design with clear living/sleeping zones
Reviews praise the cleanliness and attentive staff
Rain shower and well-laid-out bathroom for the price
cons: Limited rooms — fills up fast on weekends and holidays
No pool — this is a walk-the-town base, not a resort

entries.name: Dhevaraj Hotel
entries.revCount: 407 reviews · the most-reviewed in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Nan · next to the market, Sumon Thewarat Rd
entries.addr: 466 Sumon Thewarat Rd, Nai Wiang, Mueang Nan
entries.storyHtml: Dhevaraj is a long-running hotel locals know well, and the most-reviewed in this list with 407 reviews, scoring 9.0. It sits central, right by the market on Sumon Thewarat Road, so getting around is easy — and it has parking, which matters a lot if you've driven up. The building is older but there are renovated rooms to choose from. Real reviews praise the central location and accessible price, making it an easy, no-fuss base for exploring Nan town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a renovated Deluxe over an older-wing Standard for better value, and ask for a room away from the street so the early-morning market bustle doesn't wake you.
pros: Most-reviewed in the list, 407 reviews — lots of real data
Central location next to the market, easy to get around
On-site parking, good for those driving up
Accessible starting price for a central hotel
cons: Older building — some Standard rooms feel dated
Choose a renovated room or it may feel older than expected

entries.name: PuaDeView Boutique Resort
entries.revCount: 17 reviews · rice & mountain views in Pua
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pua district · near Wat Phra That Beng Sakat, terraced rice views
tags: 🛕 Near Wat Phra That Beng Sakat
entries.storyHtml: PuaDeView is a boutique resort built around the stepped rice terraces and mountain views of Pua district, scoring 9.2. Every room has a balcony facing the fields and hills, and there's a pool — rare at this price. It sits near Wat Phra That Beng Sakat and makes a good launch point for heading up Doi Phu Kha or touring Pua. Real reviews single out the morning views with mist rolling in and the resort's quiet atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Waking up to the rice fields under morning mist is the highlight here, and if your budget stretches, the Suite Pool Access lets you step straight from your door into the pool.
pros: Every room has a rice/mountain-view balcony — full Pua scenery
Has a pool — rare at this price point
Near Wat Phra That Beng Sakat, easy launch for touring Pua
Reviews praise the misty morning views and quiet atmosphere
cons: In Pua, about 60 km from Nan town — you need a vehicle
Few reviews so far, less data to base a decision on than in-town hotels

entries.name: Phukananan Resort
entries.revCount: 9 reviews · riverside villas in Bo Kluea
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bo Kluea district · near the ancient salt wells, mountain road
entries.addr: 295 Moo 1, Ban Bo Luang, Bo Kluea Tai, Bo Kluea
entries.storyHtml: Phukananan is a riverside villa resort tucked into the Bo Kluea valley, scoring 9.1. The draw is the riverside villas with balconies and bathtubs, where you fall asleep to the stream at night. It sits near the ancient salt wells — the district's signature sight — and makes a good base for the Bo Kluea–Sapan route. There are also budget dome rooms for travellers watching their wallet. Real reviews praise the riverside atmosphere and the privacy.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The dome rooms are cheap but small with an outdoor bathroom, so for the full riverside experience pick a Riverside Villa — and pack a warm layer, the nights get cold up here.
pros: Riverside villas with a private Bo Kluea valley feel
Near the ancient salt wells, good base for the Bo Kluea–Sapan route
Budget dome rooms available for tighter wallets
Reviews praise the quiet and the mountain views
cons: In Bo Kluea, far from Nan town on winding roads — you need a vehicle
Dome rooms are small with a separate outdoor bathroom, not for everyone

entries.name: Hugpua Hotel
entries.revCount: 14 reviews · wooden hotel in central Pua
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pua district · central Pua, near rice-view cafés
entries.storyHtml: Hugpua is a Tai Lue–style wooden hotel right in the centre of Pua district, scoring 9.0. The building is finished in wood for a warm Lanna–Tai Lue feel; rooms aren't large but are well laid out. Being central in Pua, it's a short walk or drive to the rice-view cafés and sights around the district — unlike the rice-view resorts that usually sit outside town. Real reviews praise the woodwork and the convenience of a central Pua location, making it a fit for those who want to tour Pua without long drives.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Being central, it's handy for grabbing breakfast on foot — but if waking up to rice fields outside your window matters most, this isn't that; choose based on whether you value location or the view.
pros: Tai Lue wood styling, warm and full of character
Central Pua location, easy for food and touring the district
Near Pua's well-known rice-view cafés
Clean, well-arranged rooms at an accessible price
cons: In the town centre — no direct rice view from the room
Rooms aren't large, better for couples or small groups than big families

entries.name: Nan Boutique Resort
entries.revCount: 13 reviews · rice views near Nan airport
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phu Phiang district · near Nan airport, rice views
entries.addr: 301 Moo 8, Fai Kaeo, Phu Phiang district
entries.storyHtml: Nan Boutique Resort is a rice-view resort on the Phu Phiang side, near Nan airport, scoring 8.9. The standout is space — every room runs to 55 sqm, and some are standalone villas with a small kitchen, ideal for families who want room to spread out. It's a touch outside town but close to the airport, handy if you're flying in or out early. Real reviews praise the generous room size and the quiet atmosphere around the resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group or with kids, look at the villa units with a small kitchen — and if you've got an early flight out, being this close to the airport means less buffer time needed.
pros: Spacious 55 sqm rooms throughout — lots of room for the price
Standalone villa units with a small kitchen, good for families
Near Nan airport, convenient for early arrivals/departures
Quiet rice-view setting around the resort
cons: Starting price is notably higher than in-town hotels
Outside the town centre — you'll drive to reach the Old City

entries.name: Paknap Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nai Wiang · near Nan bus terminal
entries.addr: 7/94-95 Chao Fa Rd, Nai Wiang, Mueang Nan
entries.storyHtml: Paknap is an in-town hostel that scores a strong 9.0, starting at ฿360 a bed. Dorms come with bed curtains, charging points and lockers, there's a women-only Lady Dorm, and private rooms for those who want more privacy. It sits near the Nan bus terminal — very handy if you arrive by coach. Real reviews praise the cleanliness and the friendly staff, making it a fit for backpackers and solo travellers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Solo women travellers can pick the Lady Dorm for peace of mind, and if there are two of you, compare the Private 1 Queen — it may work out better than booking two dorm beds.
pros: Lowest starting price among the private-room options, from ฿360
Dorms have curtains, charging points and lockers, well arranged
Women-only Lady Dorm · private rooms also available
Near the bus terminal, handy if you arrive by coach
cons: It's a hostel — dorms share space with other guests
Basic facilities, no pool or hotel-style services

entries.name: Nan Boutique Hotel
entries.revCount: 86 reviews · vintage style in central Nan
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nai Wiang · Khuang Luang Rd, central Nan
entries.addr: 1/11 Khuang Luang Rd, Nai Wiang, Mueang Nan
entries.storyHtml: Nan Boutique Hotel is a vintage-styled boutique in central Nai Wiang, scoring 8.6 across 86 reviews. Rooms start at 32 sqm — larger than many in-town hotels — decorated in a warm vintage tone, with Deluxe and Family rooms for groups. It sits on Khuang Luang Road in the centre, within reach of the main sights on foot. Real reviews praise the room size and decor, though some note service isn't as consistent as the top boutiques in this list — which is why it lands here.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The 32 sqm Boutique room is already roomy, but for three people or with kids, step up to a 50 sqm Deluxe/Family room for a far more comfortable stay.
pros: Roomy from 32 sqm up, warm vintage decor
Central Nai Wiang location, walkable to the sights
Deluxe/Family rooms available for groups
A fair sample of 86 reviews to weigh up
cons: Some reviews note service isn't always consistent
Overall score sits a little below the list's top boutiques

entries.name: CuteinNan Hostel
entries.revCount: 120 reviews · cute dorm in the Old City
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old City Nan · town centre, near the walking street

rooms.type: Whole room for a large group

entries.addr: 13/6 Monthian Rd, Nai Wiang, Mueang Nan
entries.storyHtml: CuteinNan is a cute dorm hostel right in the heart of Nan's Old City, starting at ฿99 a bed, with a healthy 120 reviews and a 8.7 score. What backpackers love: free bikes to borrow, perfect for pedalling to the temples and the walking street since it's so central. Dorm beds come with curtains, power points and lockers. Real reviews praise the budget price, the easy-to-walk location and the friendly vibe — a fit for budget solo travellers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Borrow a free bike and explore the Old City early before the sun gets harsh, and if you're a group, booking the whole room works out cheaper and more private than separate dorm beds.
pros: Lowest starting price in the list, ฿99 a bed
Free bikes to borrow, easy to tour the Old City
Heart-of-Old-City location, walk to the walking street
Plenty of reviews (120) · friendly atmosphere
cons: Shared dorm — limited privacy unless you book the whole room
High-season/long-weekend rates rise noticeably above ฿99

entries.name: The Impress Nan Hotel
entries.revCount: 93 reviews · large hotel, applied Lanna style
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nan town · Yantarakitkoson Rd, near Khuang Mueang
entries.addr: 4/99 Yantarakitkoson Rd, Du Tai, Mueang Nan
entries.storyHtml: The Impress is a large applied-Lanna-style hotel in Nan town, scoring 7.9 across 93 reviews and starting at just ฿900. Its strengths are scale — lots of rooms, easy parking, and the capacity to handle tour groups — making it an easy fallback when smaller boutiques are full during festivals. Real reviews are mixed: praise for the price and parking, but some note the rooms and fittings are showing their age, which is why it sits at the foot of this list. It's a fit for people who prioritise availability and parking over design.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Step up to a Deluxe, which is better finished than the Standard, and consider this place if you're travelling in numbers or need guaranteed parking.
pros: Low starting price of ฿900 for a 4-star
Large hotel with many rooms — easy availability during festivals
Easy parking, handles groups and tour parties
In-town location, convenient for getting out and about
cons: Lowest score in the list — reviews note rooms are aging
Function over design — not an atmosphere-led stay

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Nan hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Nan?
faq.a: It depends on which zone you'll explore · Old City / Nai Wiang suits temples, the museum and the walking street, all walkable (Nan Nakara, Dhevaraj, Nan Boutique, CuteinNan, Paknap) · Pua district suits stepped rice-terrace views and heading up Doi Phu Kha (PuaDeView, Hugpua) · Bo Kluea suits the Bo Kluea–Sapan route (Phukananan) · Pua and Bo Kluea are far from town, so you'll need a vehicle.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Nan hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: hostels and dorms from about ฿99–360 a bed · boutiques and in-town hotels around ฿900–1,500 · rice-view resorts in Pua from about ฿1,000 · spacious resorts/villas around ฿2,400–3,800 · During the cool season and long weekends prices rise and rooms fill fast, especially in Pua and Bo Kluea.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a vehicle in Nan, and how essential is it?
faq.a: If you're only doing the Old City, you can walk or cycle (some places lend free bikes) · But to reach Pua (about 60 km from town) or Bo Kluea (about 80 km on winding roads), a vehicle is almost essential, since public transport is very limited · Renting a car or motorbike is the most practical and flexible option.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Nan hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, booking 2–3 weeks ahead is fine · But during the cool season (November–January) and long weekends, Nan stays — especially rice-view resorts in Pua and villas in Bo Kluea — fill up fast; book 1–2 months ahead or more.

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay in Pua or in Nan town?
faq.a: Staying in Nan town suits temples, the museum, the walking street and easy access to everything · Staying in Pua suits travellers who prioritise the stepped rice views, Doi Phu Kha and the rice-view cafés — but Pua is about 60 km from town. On a multi-day trip, many people stay in Nan town for 1–2 nights, then move up to Pua for a night.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Nan hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion and period, so we recommend opening all 3 to compare before every booking — each review page in this article gives you the price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night.
